utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes, Mr. Krgovic. Yes, Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Haynes will join us tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: A little later today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. On the Prosecution side I notice Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Good morning to you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope you had a relaxing weekend. We'll continue with your testimony today. I don't think we will finish with you today. So -- but we will do our best to finish with your evidence as quickly as we can. Mr. Thayer will continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Before we continuing discussing your activities of the 13th of July, I just want to clarify one area, if I could. You testified last Friday that no Jahorina units stayed in Potocari on the night of the 12th of July. And that's at page 8608, lines 22 to 24 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I don't think they spent the night there between the 12th and 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So do you recall approximately how many Jahorina members remained along the communication on the night of 12 July? If you don't remember approximate numbers, perhaps, if you could tell the Trial Chamber, in your recollection, how many platoons, to your recollection, were left on the communication during the evening of 12 July.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact number. On Friday I gave you a rough idea of the number. I know that on the 12th of July at night there was an order, according to which another platoon should be added to the communication. Another platoon from the base that we were billeted at went to provide security of that section of that communication, which part, I don't know. I don't know whether there were six platoons in total, but all I know is that extra platoon went -- secured the communication or road. In addition to the other men, there must have been around 200 then, give or take a few. I can't be precise. As to who went with them, I think that one of the instructors and the platoon command went to the road. As to who the platoon commander was, I cannot remember that either now, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's turn to the 13th of July, please. Did you still have your radio on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I had the radio with me throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall seeing any separations of Muslim men from their families on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall receiving any reports of that happening on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any civilians abused, hit, kicked or pushed towards or on to any of the buses on the 13th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall receiving any reports of that happening on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any Muslim men directed towards or placed in any detention centres located around the UN base on the 13th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall receiving any reports of that happening on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing or having any contact with Momir Nikolic on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall having contact or conversations with any VRS officers on the 13th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, on the 13th of July, did you receive any reports of Muslims surrendering or being captured along that communication that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't receive such information, but I did hear that they surrendered, that they were captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, what did you hear, and do you recall when you heard it, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember when I heard about this, but I received information according to which that night, between the 12th and 13th, some of the Muslim forces surrendered. As to what happened to them, believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you receive any information in terms of where these Muslims surrendered or where they were taken once they were captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they surrendered in the vicinity of the road. As to where they were taken to, I didn't know. And then later I received information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "Later I received information," to what are you referring, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard that that had happened, that's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told me and an OTP investigator, just the night before you began testifying here, that you left Potocari on the 13th of July to go somewhere. Can you please tell the members of the Trial Chamber what you told us you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in the afternoon I set off in the direction of Bijeljina, and that by the road I saw a certain number of dead people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if I could just interrupt you right there, please --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And their effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may enter private session just for a little while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that a group of Muslims that had been captured or had surrendered had been placed in that hangar and that an attack had been launched or, rather, an attempt to take away the rifles from those men who had been captured by the Deputy Commander of the Sekovici platoon. There was a fight, and afterwards the people who had been captured were eliminated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. First, sir, when do you recall receiving this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate for Their Honours approximately how soon after these events that you heard occurred happened, did you find this out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. The information was relayed rapidly. There were these rumours that spread very rapidly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you say whether it was a matter of hours versus a matter of days versus a matter of weeks, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say how fast, but the territory is a fairly confined territory, so it spreads very quickly. I think it's a matter of hours or a day at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall who informed you about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I hate to interrupt, but I believe if my colleague takes a look at the transcript, I believe it needs some clarification, because here on page 6, line 14, says that an attack had been launched or rather an attempt to take away the rifles from those men who had been captured. And it doesn't make much sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he is 100 per cent right, so if you could address that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Absolutely, I'm intending to elicit more detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's go back and let me ask you a few more questions concerning what you heard about this incident at the Kravica hangar. The -- first, the transcript indicates the Sekovici platoon. What, if you remember, was the unit that you heard was involved in this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which unit was involved, but as far as I did know they mentioned the Sekovici detachment. As to whether there were any other units or men there, believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may move into private session for one question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember what I -- according to what I heard, I think there was an attempt to take away the rifles from that officer, or rather the Deputy Commander of the Sekovici detachment. And then all the other things that happened, happened. There was a fight as a result of the rifle, and what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you hear any story or account of any injuries suffered by that Deputy Commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently he burnt his hand when grabbing the barrel and so on. Believe me, I don't know. I heard that he was grabbing the barrel with his hand when he was attacked. I don't know whether fire was opened on that occasion or not, but he just grabbed the barrel. And if he burnt his hand I can assume that the barrel was hot, as they say.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you told whether any of the prisoners survived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that, no, you weren't told; or, no, prisoners survived from what you were told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I didn't hear anything about whether anyone survived or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, did you ever speak with that Deputy Commander or any other members of the unit that was deployed there about those events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, sir, believe me. Perhaps, but I can't remember, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was the overall commander on the ground of that unit at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, this is my fault. I apologise, if we could have a redaction at lines 19 and 20 of page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may move into private session just briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you had testified a short while ago about leaving Potocari and travelling home. Can you tell the Trial Chamber approximately how long you recall being absent from your duties in Potocari on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was between five and six hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall you left -- whether you left on that trip before or after the transportations had ended on the 13th of July, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think I set off in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, leaving your post for several hours during the middle of the Srebrenica operation doesn't sound like an insignificant detail. Do you have any explanation for why you failed to mention this trip in your OTP interview or during your testimony in the prior trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I'm trying to remember all the details now too, to the extent that it's possible. I'm trying to remember all the events because -- well, first of all, for my own sake, and because I'm here for the sake of my testimony, and in order to shed light on everything that happened down there. Because I'm now a witness at the International Tribunal, and everything I state could appear at some other court, and could serve to accuse me of having acted in a certain way. I'm trying to remember everything I can, to the extent that that is possible. Much time has passed since all those things happened, so I'm simply trying to remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, do you recall approximately what time of day it was when you returned home from this -- or when you left home after this trip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where did you return after this trip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to where we were billeted at Bjelovac in school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on the night of the 13th of July, were any Jahorina or regular special brigade or PJP members, to your knowledge, assigned to guard duties in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll take it one piece at a time then. On the 13th of July, sir, were any Jahorina units assigned to any guard duties in or around the town of Bratunac, excluding the communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, not in Bratunac. Around Bratunac, along the road, I believe that there was just one unit or detachment of the deserters from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, same question with respect to regular special police brigade or PJP members. Do you have any knowledge as to whether any of those units were assigned to guard duties in the town or immediately around the town of Bratunac, excluding the communication?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour, because of the complexity of the question. When you mentioned PJP, that entails six companies that are at the time located in or around Bratunac, so this question is ill-defined and very complex.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't question whether it is complex or not, but I think the witness, on Friday, repeatedly referred to various units including the PJP units. If he thinks that the question is too complex, he can't answer it, then we'll ask Mr. Thayer of course to be more specific. But if the witness can answer it, I think he should go ahead. Witness, have you followed the conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think you are in a position to answer Mr. Thayer's question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I answered to the best of my knowledge. I believe that units from Jahorina were placed along the communication. Whether the Sekovici detachment was there, where they were supposed to be, I don't know. Who was deployed elsewhere, well, that I, believe me, do not know which units were deployed in the rest of the territory. That I do not know, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll just leave it there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the night of 13th of July, were you aware that thousands of prisoners were being held in Bratunac, in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. That brings us to the 14th of July, sir. Did you receive any reports that day about any Jahorina unit members being injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received reports that three members from Jahorina had been wounded along that communication road. I don't know which section, that there was an assault, that a grenade had been thrown at them and that those who had thrown the grenade had fled. I don't know how they were transported to the hospital. I think in the evening of -- I don't know which day -- went to the hospital to visit them. I found them in the Zvornik hospital. Maybe on the 14th or the 15th in the evening, I'm not sure which. It could have been the 16th. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall where you actually slept on the evening of the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I slept at Bjelovac, as far as I can remember, the place where we were billeted at.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Trial Chamber what, if anything, you recall doing on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been given tasks to continue securing the communication, and I spent some time in Bjelovac. I divided my time between Bjelovac and Bratunac. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, sir, when you refer to being given tasks to continue securing the communication, who gave you those tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you referred to a meeting with Mr. Borovcanin and a -- according to the transcript, Mr. Dervenic. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I want to turn your attention to the 16th of July, sir. At some point on that day did you receive another order from Mr. Borovcanin about the patrols along the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was given an order to withdraw men from the communication to form patrols and to use the BRDM vehicle from the public security station of Bratunac and a jeep and to patrol the communication. Since the BRDM vehicle was out of repair, we couldn't use it. We used a Pinzgauer and the jeep to patrol the security of the communication in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what is a BRDM and what are you referring to when you speak about a Pinzgauer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pinzgauer is an off-road vehicle for soldiers' transportation and BRDM is an armoured vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall receiving any other orders on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the 16th, in the evening, I believe it was, I was ordered to report to Major Nikolic to search and comb the area. In the evening hours, maybe in -- around 2300 hours, I met Major Nikolic at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. He told me that the briefing was supposed to be next morning between 8.00 and 9.00 at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters, and to be given tasks about our and their tasks within the combing -- to comb the area and the territory. In the morning I went to the Bratunac Brigade command headquarters. I am not sure who chaired the briefing, but I know that tasks had been arranged and we divided up the territory and, as they say, we were given pieces of territory to search and the deployment of both military and police units. We had Sapas to demine the areas and from the police side we had units with guard dogs, search dogs and we were given tasks. We distributed maps, we were given tasks, we arranged for a communication methods and on the 17th we were supposed to start combing the area at 10.00 in the morning. But we were delayed and I can't remember when we started from the departure point. I can't remember which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me just stop you right there, sir. Turning your attention back to the 16th of July, for just a moment, who gave you the order to meet with Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I think there was an order, and I know that I met Mr. Borovcanin on -- in the evening of the 16th. Whether this order emanated from somebody else or -- I don't know. Could have been it was an order of the brigade commander's, Mr. Saric's. This is what I know when it comes to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. But who personally ordered you to go to Bratunac and meet Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, at that time, sir, do you recall who else personally could have given you that order on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Saric could have done that. He was a brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was Mr. Saric on the ground at this time, in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him, but I received information that he had arrived to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, turning your attention, sir, back to the 17th of July and this searching of the terrain operation. Do you recall who from the Bratunac Brigade was represented at the meeting? And if you don't recall particular people, do you recall what their positions were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the names of the people and, to be frank, I cannot recall their positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall who gave you the order at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters on the 17th of July to go out and conduct this search operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the officer who chaired the briefing did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this officer a member of the Bratunac Brigade or was this person a member of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I received an order to search the area at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, sir, did that order come from a member of the Bratunac Brigade or a member of some other unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clarify that question for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: On the 17th of July, sir, at the meeting at the Bratunac Brigade, when you received the final order to commence the search operation, once the parameters of the operation had been decided and worked out, do you recall who gave you that order? If you can't remember the individual's name, can you tell the Trial Chamber what unit that individual belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that exactly, sir. I know that I attended that meeting at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters. I know that we were given tasks, that we were given maps and that we agreed on a method of reporting and that we set out to perform that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember whether the order came from a VRS officer as opposed to a MUP officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, sir, believe me. I know that this meeting took place and it unfolded the way that I explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe what you did on this operation, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we simply combed the area. We were on the look-out for Muslim forces in the area. We went through the area to check whether there were -- well, this is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you take any prisoners or did anyone surrender to you during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening hours I said that some 200 Muslims and four children had surrendered. I don't know at which location exactly. And I know that they -- that children were given to the care of Captain Gavric and that the rest were transported in the direction of Konjevic Polje. Whether there were fewer or more than 200, I would be mistaken if I were to speculate. I know that, as far as I can recall, some people were detailed to provide security on behalf of military and police, and

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may go into private session for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sure. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this clip that the ran at 2 hours, 26 minutes, 51 seconds to 2 hours, 26 minutes, and 55 seconds, there is an individual at the left of the screen. Can you identify what unit that individual belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the deserters' unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll move along.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're going to skip a clip to save a little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, do you recognise anybody in this clip which began at 2 hours, 29 minutes, 45 seconds and ended at 2 hours, 29 minutes, 57.9 seconds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise Mr. Borovcanin and the young man in the blue flak jacket, who was a member of the deserters' unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And for the record, Mr. Borovcanin is to the immediate left of the flak jacket, the man in the flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're going to skip another clip to save a little time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this clip which began at 2 hours, 37 minutes, 43 seconds and ended at 2 hours and 38 minutes, can you identify the unit from which this individual, in the centre of the image, is from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you sharpen the image a bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can replay it, certainly. And, sir, for each of these videotape clips, did I also show you a still photograph based on that clip at my office last week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did that help at all, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is a member of the special police brigade. That's how I would identify him on the basis of this image. Because of the insignia that they had on their uniforms on the sleeves of their uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this clip which began at 2 hours, 39 minutes and 21 seconds and ended at 2 hours, 39 minutes and 43.7 seconds, can you identify the unit to which the individual in the immediate foreground of this image belongs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was a member of the special police brigade within the Sekovici detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you referred to a patch or insignia previously and with respect to the individual in the clip we just saw before this one, do you see that patch as well in this image?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where is that patch, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On his left sleeve of his uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, having just viewed this clip, including a slow-motion version, the clip beginning at 2 hours, 39 minutes, 54 seconds and ending at 2 hours, 40 minutes and 11 seconds, do you recognise that location just depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. I had the opportunity of seeing some of the Muslims who had surrendered on the 12th or on the 13th. I know that on that occasion those who had surrendered were on a sort of plateau; it was like a slight elevation. As far as I can remember, at the time when that group surrendered, General Mladic also spoke to them. As for the exact location, well, I don't know where it was, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So let me ask you, to the best of your recollection, as you sit here today, do you recognise the location that was just depicted in that video clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to answer that question. I remember this detail. I know that I personally saw a group that surrendered, and I think that at that time it was on a plateau, and I think that General Mladic and perhaps others spoke to them. I don't know, whatever I said, if -- might be doubtful, I can't remember very well. I know that at the road that was secured by the unit from Jahorina, I know there was a -- the road secured by the unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll move along then.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This clip which began at 2 hours, 47 minutes and has ended at 2 hours, 47 minutes and 22 seconds, can you identify from what unit this individual holding the automatic rifle belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the deserters' unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at 2 hours, 47 minutes and 51.5 seconds, can you recognise what unit this individual wearing the gloves was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the deserters' unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We're going to skip ahead a little bit, try to save some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone by name or by unit in this clip at 2 hours, 49 minutes and 17.4 seconds, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recognise Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that's it; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recognise him, but not the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now at 2 hours, 49 minutes and 20.9 seconds, do you recognise the unit or this particular individual by name in the purple shirt in the middle of the image, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recognise this man in the T-shirt, but I think he is part of the special police brigade, because he had such a uniform on him, although he had taken the upper part off. He had this characteristic jump suit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Moving along.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at 2 hours, 49 minutes and 37.9 seconds, do you recognise the unit of this individual?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the deserters' unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at 2 hours, 49 minutes and 45.5 seconds, do you recognise the unit of this individual with the automatic rifle pointed down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the deserters' unit from Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, having seen this clip, which is stopped at 2 hours, 50 minutes, 17.3 seconds, do you recognise anyone depicted in this still?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recognise Mr. Borovcanin here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And he's standing next to the man in the blue helmet. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We'll skip ahead to the last clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this clip which began at 2 hours, 56 minutes and has stopped at 2 hours, 56 minutes, 25.4 seconds, can you identify what unit the individual depicted in the far right of this image belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the jump suit, he could be a member of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, just a couple of more questions before I conclude. Sir, did you discipline -- Your Honour, if we may move into private session out of an abundance of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Just one moment, because I need to make a further annotation. Yes, who's going first? I would imagine Mr. Stojanovic. Take as much time as you require. At the same time, please try not to be repetitive. Yeah, we can take the break now. I mean we've only got three hours [sic] more for the break. We can take the break now. And then it will be your turn. Three minutes. Because as you realise, time really flies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just before we start with the cross-examination, I'd like to inform you that I forwarded to the registry the list of documents for identification awaiting translation. They're now translated into English and they are available on e-court. I've told the Prosecutor which documents they were. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much for your efforts, Madam Fauveau. And we can proceed. Who is going first? I suppose Mr. Stojanovic for Borovcanin. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to have the first five questions answered in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will do that. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a document entitled, "Report of the work of the Ministry of the Interior for 1995." It is in the system, but unfortunately it has not been translated. We are going to use one paragraph on page 4 of this report, and I would like to see page 4, central section of page 4. And I believe that we will receive a simultaneous interpretation of that sentence as we read it. So this is page 2. Let us go to page 4. Thank you. This is it, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let us take a look at the central section of this page, which reads, "Team of instructors of the special police brigade conducted training with 202 military conscripts at Jahorina over two months. In July, the training centre Jahorina was established, where 235 military conscripts are being trained from two generations that are doing their military service in the MUP units." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can we then agree that this training centre, which is called Jahorina, in terms of establishment, it was not part of the special police brigade in July, but within the structure of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell you, it was part of the special police brigade, and what is stated here is correct. And I was -- managed this centre on behalf of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did deserters, who were taken there in June 1995, belong to the special brigade or were they just instructors who were conducting the training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Deserters were members of the training centre, and if the centre belonged to the brigade, then it follows that the members belonged to the brigade as well. And the instructors that conducted the training and the courses were from the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that military conscripts were trained at this training centre, so young soldiers who were not members of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were two generations of young conscripts. At this time there was this law in force. One group was around 30 to 40 strong, and the other group of conscripts was larger and they were sent to do their training at this centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: After having completed their training, the participants were then deployed and sent to different military units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as military conscripts were concerned, I do not know where they were deployed. Later on, as far as participants at Kusici are concerned, I do not know where they were deployed afterwards either, but as far as the deserters' unit is concerned, I remember that it was deployed in the special police brigades and deployed throughout the territory of Republika of Srpska, at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that these deserters, as you dubbed them, started arriving at the centre from the 19th of June, 1995, onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know exactly when they started arriving, but I know that they would spend a short time in training, maybe two, two and a half months, maybe longer, maybe shorter period of time, but believe me, I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did they arrive en masse or was this a process where they would be coming in waves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, I think it was a process, they did not arrive en masse, but I cannot tell you how long this period of gathering them at the centre lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: These were not professional policemen, they do not have official MUP ID, and they were not paid by the MUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, I want to make sure that -- in other words he is saying that there were not professional policemen because there are two questions. And they were not paid by the MUP. Answer to both questions is yes, that they were not professional policemen and that they were not paid by the MUP. You confirmed these two propositions that have been put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you wish me, I can explain. To be a professional policeman, you first have to graduate from either a course or a police academy. They had not attended such training. They attended only the military part of their training, physical exercise and the basic part of military training. But they did belong to the police. I am not sure whether they had official MUP IDs. I think they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who paid them? From which ministry or organisation were they paid from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Only the Ministry of Interior could have paid them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I put the question whether he had answered yes to one or both. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you permit me, let us clarify another thing. On Friday, when discussing the structure of special police brigade, you said that there was a mixed anti-armour and artillery division. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that in the structure of the special police brigade this organisational form that anti-armour and artillery division, was established in October 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know when it was established, but it existed in the structure, whether it existed in June 1995, I don't know, believe me, but it is possible it was established later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You said in -- during your examination-in-chief that on the 11th of July you received an order to take a company from Jahorina and to go towards Bratunac. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you leave a possibility for that order to be received at the centre through official channels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot recall that, believe me. If I were to tell you exactly, I couldn't, because I can't remember. The only way for it to arrive would be through official channels, but I cannot recall how it arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Later on we are going to take a look at that order, and we will be able to confirm what you have just said. Can you recall at which time were you -- you became familiar with this order dated 10th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know when exactly, but I know that I met Mr. Borovcanin and he relayed that order orally to me, but I cannot tell you exactly the date or the time of day. I really cannot pin-point that for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand you fully, but I tried to eliminate any ambiguity as to whether it was on the 10th or the 11th of July, given that the date of the order was the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was contacted and when I met Mr. Borovcanin, I know that I was ordered to move my unit, and in my opinion that could have been on the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've had opportunity to hear one witness of the Prosecution who described a person who had attended the course. The person who issued this order and who addressed them as a man of -- middle-aged man of middle height, he was the commander of all the special police units. Could you tell us from this description who that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was commander of all special units, that would be Mr. Saric. But I cannot recall whether somebody addressed the attendants or not. I really cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Before departure, members of that company from the Jahorina training centre were given uniforms, as you've said, automatic weapons, and a certain number of blue flak jackets made in Israel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let us take a look together at a photograph. At a photograph, I believe that we've had the opportunity to see it. Your Honour, P01936. P01936, page 61. ERN is 0364-7881. Before we see it on the screen, sir, I'd like to refresh your memory. At one point, when asked to recognise certain persons, you described a member of, as you called them, the deserters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if you have been able to follow, but there is a problem if we show the picture as it is, unfortunately, in the system, it also has -- it also shows a name. So I'm trying to see, before it is broadcast, whether we could have the technicians zoom in and eliminate the name from the screen so that we can proceed without any problems. Yes, Mr. Thayer. Do you have a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have hard copies that we can obscure if Your Honour's suggestion doesn't work out. So we have an alternative available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. But I think we have had this problem before and it did work out. No, it cannot be done without the witness seeing it, actually. Do you have a copy of it yourselves? It's not in colour; it's in black and white. Is it okay with you? The name -- the name doesn't show on that document, does it? Shall we put it on the ELMO. That's clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Stojanovic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the photograph? It is in black and white.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: A minute ago, you said or, rather, you had an opportunity, to see this image as part of a video clip. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The individual marked with number 2 is one you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree that the flak jacket on this individual is, in fact, the Israeli light blue flak jacket that were issued to these men when they set off from Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So these flak jackets are not the flak jackets worn by members of the Dutch battalion on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can now remove the photograph from the ELMO. Thank you. Your next meeting with Mr. Borovcanin, as you said on Friday, was held on the 11th of July when you arrived in Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that is why I want to put this question to you. Can you tell us if it was on the 11th of July that you met, at what time did you meet Mr. Borovcanin in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, by 1500 hours we had arrived in the village where we found accommodation, so it must have been -- or it could have been in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's try and be a little more precise for the sake of the following question. Was it immediately upon your arrival or a certain time after you had arrived there and found accommodation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that we first arrived there, found accommodation, and then I saw Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If I said that in the afternoon of the 11th of July, 1995, Ljubomir Borovcanin was at forward command post at Pribicevac, would you be less certain that that meeting was yours was on the afternoon on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I had that meeting after we had found accommodation, but as to when it was exactly, believe me, I can't be certain. I know we arrived there, we found accommodation, and then we had a meeting with him. But as for the precise time, I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to ask my learned friend for a time reference for his question, given that he is seeking a specific time. But the witness went ahead and answered the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know if I should insist on the time, because I believe that the witness has told me everything he can as far as the time is concerned, it was after 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can move ahead with your next question. That's what Mr. Thayer actually said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Then, sir, you went to reconnoitre the wide Potocari area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would it refresh your memory if I told you that you were the cock out of the hill at the time, the hill above the Yellow Bridge and the observation post manned by UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the name of the hill was, but there was certainly on some hill, at some elevation to the right, or rather to the right of Bratunac when you come from Konjevic Polje, but I don't know what the name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We've been following the transcript, so let's just try to deal with this once more. You said to the right of the road when you look from Bratunac in the direction of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hill was somewhere on the route from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, so when you observe from the hill you have the Potocari base, and Potocari. And you have the Yellow Bridge. I can't really say where it was exactly, you know, but I was involved in carrying out reconnaissance there, there's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And there's no doubt about the fact that you could see the UN base from the hill, you could see the observation post, and the Yellow Bridge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could certainly see the UN base. I think I could also see the Yellow Bridge, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then you received a new task: On the 12th of July you were to provide security for the UN base. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That meant to protect the property and the people in the base from potential attacks. Is that how you understood your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is -- well, whether the task was described in that way, I don't know, but that's how I understood it. That's how I interpreted it. That's how I saw it. I didn't know what else I could do with UNPROFOR members, and I wasn't going to capture them, keep them in detention. That's how I understood my task, and that's how I approached it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is, in fact, what we will ask you about, and after you had left the Yellow Bridge that morning on the 12th, you passed by the UN observation post, if you remember. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, the UN observation post was in the vicinity of the Yellow Bridge, or the Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You passed by the observation post, and you did not linger there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember whether we stopped there, but we passed by that area. Perhaps we had contact with the men, perhaps we had some discussions, but I can't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There was no fighting or no exchange of fire between you and the members of the Dutch battalion at that post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you did not arrest a single UN member at that observation post?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to confirm, are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just wanted to confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We were in private session only for the first five questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, I think you need to repeat your answer. And the question -- because the interpreters didn't catch it. The question was, "And you did not arrest a single UN member at that observation post?" And what was your answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not answer the question. It didn't even cross our minds. It didn't cross my mind to arrest a member of the United Nations. I wouldn't even dream of doing something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Upon arriving in Potocari, you didn't fight with members of the Dutch battalion in the UN base either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, we didn't have conflicts of any kind. The men I met were men with whom I was on very decent terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you personally aware of any members of your unit who entered the area of Potocari at the time? Are you aware of them arresting members of the Dutch battalion or of disarming them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any information, you personally, according to which during that period Ljubomir Borovcanin acted wilfully in the Drina Corps territory, regardless of the orders from his superiors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, I don't believe that he acted wilfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to deal with questions that concern the police and the army. Could we have a look at P00725, please, a Prosecution exhibit. Your Honours, this is a law or it's an application of the law on defence in imminent threat of war during the state of war. It was published in the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska 1 through 94. It was a special edition and I think we will often be using this Official Gazette. If we could just have a look at it. Let's have a look at page 2 of the Official Gazette, article 3 from the top in the B/C/S version, and page 3, paragraph 2, in the English version of this law. Could we have both versions side by side so that we can follow this, since I will be dealing with these provisions. Let's just focus on Article 2 or paragraph 2 of this law. In both the B/C/S and in the English version. Article 2. Sir, let's have a look at this. I will read it out and you can follow. Article 2. Article 2 states the following: "The armed forces of Republika Srpska shall be composed of the army of Republika Srpska and MUP units from Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we are looking at the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so too. Yes, Mr. Thayer, can you help us?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think it's the next page of the English translation, which ends in 0437 of the ERN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think we now have the right English version before us. May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Now we have the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if we have a look at Article 2, Article 2 states the following: "The armed forces of Republika Srpska shall consist of the army of Republika Srpska and the units of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's now have a look at Article 3 of the same law. Which states the following: "The president of the republic is the commander in chief of the armed forces. The commander in chief of the armed forces shall establish the Supreme Command. The Supreme Command shall comprise the following: The vice-president of the republic, the president of the people's assembly of Republika Srpska, the prime minister of Republika Srpska, the Minister of Defence and the Minister of the Interior." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's have a look at a chart. 4D92. We made this chart when preparing for your cross-examination. We wanted to ask you whether it's a correct reflection of the laws we have just read out, the laws on defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'm just wondering if there is an English -- there it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we made an effort, and at the bottom it is stated that this is our translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, have a look at the chart. The armed forces of Republika Srpska consists of, as can be seen in this chart, of the army of Republika Srpska, and MUP units from Republika Srpska. That's what we read out in Article 2 of the law a minute ago. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does this chart tally with Article 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Article 3 stated that the Supreme Command of the armed forces was the president of Republika Srpska, and he formed the Supreme Command, and the Supreme Command consists of individuals or, rather, positions listed in the third margin. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can we agree that this chart corresponds to the laws, Article 2 and 3, on defence when there is an imminent threat of war or state of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we are speaking the same language, I am making pauses to enable interpretation. So bear with me. Given your police training and provisional experience and expertise, let's -- I would like to ask you to help us in explaining the functioning and the command over MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to bring back the exhibit P00725, but this time around, page 4. In the B/C/S version, which discusses the law on the application of law on the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Stojanovic. Let's wait until we get...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which page in English, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be page 12, paragraph 1 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It certainly doesn't correspond. It certainly doesn't correspond. How can it be page 4 in the B/C/S and page 12 in the English, if this is just a translation of a legal text?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see, okay. Yeah, but this is not the page anyway. I mean it's definitely not the page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 12 in the B/C/S version that you see before you, let us scroll down, please. Excellent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. So the last article on page 4 of the B/C/S version is the first article on page 12 of the English version. This is just for the record. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let us focus on Article 12, if you can see it in the bottom right corner, which reads: "Distinct from special-purpose police units, Minister of the Interior shall establish special police units to carry out combat tasks." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You discussed that. You said that there were special units of police and you said that there was a special brigade of the police. To the best of your knowledge, this would be the state of affairs in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the law was concerned, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we can have another digression, on page 47, row 15, there was a problem of interpretation when we said "special units of police". It says in the interpretation "special police units." I know that this is a very subtle distinction, but this may prove vital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am -- I'm not following. I can't follow. If I read page 47, lines 14 and 15, what we have is the following: "So let's focus on Article 12, if you can see it in the bottom right corner which reads 'distinct from special purpose police units, minister of the interior shall establish special police units to carry out combat.'" What's wrong with that? Because even if I read the text on e-court, Article 12 is there translated as, "Distinct from special-purpose police units, the minister of the interior shall establish special police units to carry out combat tasks." So obviously the two are not the same. But what I cannot understand is where is the mistake in the -- in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, Your Honour, to use my modest knowledge of English, we used this term. When we say "special unit of police," we mean by that a special police brigade. But for "special units of police," we use the English terms "separate." So I would like to ask this terminology to be used from now on, and there is no -- we both stipulate, the Prosecution and Defence about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. This is a bit of a debate I have had with CLSS for many years. They just don't want to use "separate". So I thought we had talked about using the term "PJP" to term this special purpose unit. I don't think you're going to get them to say "separate" but if we stick with PJP, I think it will be clearer. Sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you agree to that, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. We will have to make some distinctions within the PJP. But we believe that this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's another matter. Okay. So we can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let us take a look at Article 13 of this same act, on the following page in the B/C/S version, and on the same page in the English version. Sir, take a look at paragraph 2 of Article 13, which reads, "The minister of the interior shall give orders to police units through the ministry police forces command staff."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question is whether you know in July 1995 there was a police forces command staff of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that command staff did exist at the level of the Ministry of the Interior, police forces command staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to take a look at another chart, that would be Exhibit 4D93. But we are going to go back to Article 14 of this same law, so let us keep it close or nearby. So, sir, now I'm going to show you a schematic or a chart, which describes what we read about from the law. Thank you. Can you see that the command structure and direction structure, pursuant to this law, goes from the Supreme Command towards the minister, and then on through the police forces staff, as specified here in Article 13. And then later on towards the PJP and the special police brigade. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does this schematic correspond to your knowledge about the system of command and the application of the law on internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to focus on the right-hand side of the page, where we have the public security department in the box, and then from public security department orders go to public security centres. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is it known to you that in the system of command and direction in 1995, in July, that there was a command staff at the level of the public security centre at Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is it known to you that, within the public security department, there was also a public police force staff to execute certain functions within the system of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is known to me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So we can agree that this schematic corresponds to the legislative solutions that we read about a couple of minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next what I'd like to ask you about is your knowledge about the existence of more than one units of PJP from the centre of Zvornik in this area. Is it known to you that there were some units of PJP in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right. I'll try to rephrase my question. In July 1995, during the period when you were there, in that area of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Konjevic Polje, there were units of PJP that belonged to the public security centre of Zvornik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When observing this schematic, could you agree with me that the PJP companies were commanded by the public security centre of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As per this schematic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: But you have no knowledge or cannot tell us anything about the existence of a command staff at the level of the public security centre of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, and this is what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I will not ask you anything about that. Now let us go back to the law on the application of the law on internal affairs and that will be Exhibit P00725. And let us focus on page 14.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Article 14, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which are both on the same page in the English and B/C/S version. Yes, this is the correct page of the B/C/S version. And it is page 12, if I'm not very much mistaken, in the English version, and we just saw it a couple of minutes ago. Thank you. I believe this is as it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let us focus, Your Honour, on Article 14, paragraph 1 of this law. Which reads -- sir, can you follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "Police units assigned to combat operations by an order of the commander in chief of the armed forces shall be resubordinated to the commander of the unit in whose zone of responsibility they are performing their combat tasks." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that by application of Article 14, paragraph 1 of this law on the application of law on internal affairs, during the imminent threat of war or state of war, this combat unit in question that was commanded by Ljubomir Borovcanin was assigned to combat operations and that the same was resubordinated to the commander of the Drina Corps, because that was the zone, the unit whose -- in whose zone of responsibility you were performing the combat tasks? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. To make matters clearer, Your Honour, I would like to invoke Prosecution Exhibit P0094, and that, before we see it on e-court, to tell that this was the staff commander's order of police forces, 64/95 from the 10th of July, 1995. I believe that we had occasion to see this order, Your Honour. It has been translated into English. Thank you. Sir, let us take a look at this order. You've been shown it during your examination-in-chief. In the mid-section, take a look at how it starts. "Based on the order of the Supreme Commander of the Republika Srpska armed forces and in order to crush the enemy offensive from the Srebrenica protected zone..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "...I hereby order," and if you can take a look, it has been signed by the commander of the police forces staff in the bottom left corner. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It is not signed. You cannot sign -- see the sign, but we can see the name of the person who was supposed to sign it, and this is going to be discussed later on during the proceedings. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the header of this document, in the upper right corner, it says, "Very urgent ss." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In dispatch traffic, if we can seek your assistance as to what this marking meant.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very urgent would be hiding behind this marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would that, in this specific case, mean that this order was very urgent and sent to all participants specified below the date line, the 10th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be so.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the seventh line it states that this order has been forwarded to the Jahorina training camp. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does that confirm what we have already discussed, that this order, as early as the 10th of July 1995, was to be forwarded to the training camp in Jahorina, through official channels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it should have been relayed through official channels to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's now read through item 2 of the order. It's already been shown to you by the Prosecution. For sake of brevity I will just concentrate on the last words under item 2, "As part of this unit a company from the camp of the centre for training in Jahorina shall be included." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree that according to this order only one company out of two from the training centre in Jahorina was sent, on the basis of this order, to the Srebrenica area and that one company, which became part of this combat unit, had Ljubomir Borovcanin assigned to them as their commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the conclusion one can draw on the basis of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's have a look at item 5 now, which states the following: "The unit commander, Ljubomir Borovcanin, upon arriving at his destination, must establish contact with the corps Chief of Staff, General Krstic." How do you interpret this task? How do you interpret the order that Ljubomir Borovcanin received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I may put it in very simple terms, what I can say is that Mr. Borovcanin had the task of commanding and leading MUP units, and those MUP units, Ministry of the Interior units, were resubordinated through him to the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps, namely General Krstic. That's how I could interpret it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. To conclude, in this case he would receive orders from the Drina Corps command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then he would forward them through the system of command to the chain of command to you and to subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should have worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We'll see how this functioned when examining documents a little later on, but there's something else I'd like to clear up now. Upon entering Potocari on the 12th of July, 1995, were you in the vicinity of Mladic when he spoke -- you were close to Mladic when he spoke to people from Srebrenica. And we saw this in the video clip today. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can we agree that that was on the 12th of July in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: On Friday you described and sketched the way in which your unit moved from the Yellow Bridge to Potocari. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the routes we followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember that on that occasion from the left when we look in the direction you were advancing in, there was shooting, at one point in time, that didn't last for long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
