utterances.text: As far as I can remember, on arriving I think we were near that group of citizens, and to the left from the hill, as far as I can remember, fire was opened on us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree with us that the reason, for entering the UN base that you discussed on Friday, was to check whether ABiH members were present in the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Entering the UN base, the grounds of the base -- well, we entered the base to see who was there, to see whether there were any ABiH members. And it's certainly for those reasons that we entered the base. We couldn't have entered or wouldn't have entered the base for any other reasons. When we entered the base we saw a certain number of civilians, there were wounded people, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you saw that there were no ABiH members in the base, at least armed ABiH members, you immediately left the base. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We rapidly left the base. I don't think we spent more than a few minutes there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. We've already heard one member of the Dutch battalion testify about that, and corresponds to what you have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please move into private session very briefly now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly, let's move into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to have a look at a video clip V0004458. It's Prosecution document P02047 to 1241, up until 2.13.08 is the relevant time. Let's have a look at it now and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we stop there, please, for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know which military unit these soldiers belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Can we go back a little bit to where we stopped? Because we need to put the reference. Okay. Stop. So we are at 2 hours, 12 minutes, 45 seconds when the last question by Mr. Stojanovic was put. Thank you. Let's go ahead now. The question is to you, sir, "Do you know which military unit these soldiers belonged to?" And we have in the transcript that you answered "no." Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, I don't know which unit they belong to. Given their uniforms, some of these soldiers belong to the deserters' unit from Jahorina. I wouldn't put that in dispute, but I wouldn't know the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would this confirm your answer from a moment ago that there were other units at Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a huge flux of units, movement of people in both directions. I could not register the units, groups, individuals who came there. This is my impression of the goings on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we continue and stop at 2.13.08.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stop here, please. Thank you. So for identification purposes, this is 2.13.02.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, next to this bus, can you see two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know which military unit they belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are members of the military police, but I don't know which unit of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you are certain that these are not members of the unit that you came to Potocari with; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would this confirm your statement of a while ago that in Bratunac or in Potocari, on the 12th of July, there were many units that were deployed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which units were deployed there, but I am sure that there were many units. I know that I was with a part of my unit at Potocari. For the rest, I really don't know, believe me. There were many units there, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us take a look at another segment of the same video clip, 4458, which you were shown during your examination-in-chief. It starts with 2.26.02 and ends 2.26.16, so it's a 14-second extract. And could you follow the subtitles or the words and the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For reference purposes, we end at 2.26.16.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, we didn't receive audio for that clip and I don't know if that was part of the presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That was one thing. At the same time, I was watching you stand up. I thought for a moment that you were going to refer to the last part in the transcript of Mr. Stojanovic's question and could you follow the subtitles or the words and the image. We don't know, as far as I know, I speak for myself, at least, I don't know if the witness understands English or not. If he doesn't, how can he follow the -- so let's put the two together. Go back to where we started from, have the audio in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe for reference purposes we received audio in B/C/S, in the language that we understand, and I believe that the witness and everybody else following the proceedings in B/C/S could understand and hear what the participants said. But I'm not sure whether you received the interpretation. As far as Mr. Thayer said, this appears to be so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to go back to it, have it played again. And I want to make sure that the witness is receiving the audio, also us. But we can follow the captions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, could you hear what the people in the video clip said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You understand the language that they spoke?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: One of the people in the clip said to "Go around and see whether they are going. This is their job." Did you hear this being said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is, could you tell us here and now who was he addressing with these words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- he addressed the -- this lad who was part of the Jahorina deserters' unit. This is what I presume, that he is addressing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If he says, "It's their job," who is he addressing, this remark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who he is addressing, presumably other members of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The gist of my question is this: I would like to find out what is your knowledge about the role and the work of the Dutch battalion's tasks in the job of evacuating people from the Potocari base on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, the Dutch battalion, together with our people, was literally mixed with the civilians. They were securing the civilians, together with our members, to prevent a stampede, if I may use this word, when the buses arrived to evacuate the civilians. Don't take my word for it, but I believe that we formed a human chain, holding hands together, because when buses would arrive they would let a certain number of people pass to fill the buses and trucks that were headed towards Bratunac and further on. So whether the Dutch battalion coordinated a part of these efforts, well, yes, as far as I know. They were supposed to follow or escort these columns of vehicles. I don't know whether the UNHCR was supposed to escort them. Whether they escorted those columns in the direction of Konjevic Polje, Bratunac, Vlasenica, Bjelici and I can't remember the name of the town where they were heading for. I don't know whether they escorted them or not. I don't know whether UNHCR people escorted them or not. I know that they were there though, and that they were coordinating many things. They were present at the scene at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can we agree that they were practically doing the same task as your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this concerns, yes, I believe that they were doing the same task as our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I believe that this would be the right time to take a break, if I'm not very much mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are neither very much nor less mistaken. It is time to take the break. So we will have a 25-minute break starting -- is 25 minutes enough since we have a redaction? Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, we stopped while discussing the position and role of the Dutch battalion. You said that they were supposed to escort the vehicles transporting the civilians out of the base. My next question is, do you know who secured the arrival of the vehicles that transported the inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who secured the arrival of those vehicles, but as far as I know, police could not assign so many personnel to secure such a large number of vehicles to evacuate the civilians, the -- I don't know who secured those vehicles that came to evacuate the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You will agree with me that it wasn't the police as just -- you just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It couldn't be the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long did you spend at Potocari, you personally, on the day in question, on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for my forays to the road, I believe that most of my time I spent at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on Friday in -- during examination-in-chief, the witness mentioned one name. We checked and that was done in open session. I have no problem with that being done in open session, but guide me because of the position of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know which name you are referring to. Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think I know the name, Mr. President, and if we could go into private session, I may have inadvertently kept us in open for that on Friday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you remember, could you tell us, on that date, on the 12th of July, that you saw him in Potocari, did he wear a uniform or civilian clothes? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is it known to you that that person is married to a pharmacist from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- this is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that in the transcript it says a pharmacist. My question was whether he knew that that person was married to a doctor from Bratunac. Let us correct this in the transcript, because this is going to be the subject matter of some other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this would not change anything in your answer if I were to ask you whether you knew he was married to a doctor from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I told you that he was married to a woman from Bratunac, that he has a house in Bratunac, and that her relatives then and now live in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will have no further questions concerning that. Except for the incident that you mentioned on Friday concerning one of the members of your unit, did you hear of any other murders or mistreatment of civilians at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you inform Ljubomir Borovcanin of that incident or an attempt to mistreat a civilian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall whether I did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: As a superior officer, did you take any measures, discipline or criminal measures against that member of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that later on he was expelled from the unit, but I don't know the grounds for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You told us that part of the unit that you called the deserters, as early as on the 12th of July, was sent to secure the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two platoons were sent to secure the communication, and as far as I can recall, one platoon was -- stayed at Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can we agree that the -- that platoon was 30 strong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to establishment, that was supposed to be the -- the number, but I'm not sure whether it was actually 30 strong or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall when did those two platoons depart towards the communication, Sandici, Lolici, Konjevic Polje, on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that was -- how shall I put it? Between the discussion of Mr. Borovcanin and General Mladic and after General Mladic addressed the crowd, that their departure was after that. I cannot pin-point the exact time, but during that period, between that what I said and high noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know how they departed to that road that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What is the distance from Potocari to that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact mileage. Maybe 10 to 15, 20 kilometres, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When did the remainder of the deserters' unit depart for that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Company that I subsequently learnt that it had arrived, I don't know when they were sent to the road, but I do know that they joined up along that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree that this happened on the 13th, in the late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean those units departing for the -- that road?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, the remainder of the units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I know that those units joined up along that road or communication. I don't remember the exact date or exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you regardless of whether it was on the 12th or the 13th or whether the whole of the unit of the deserters went or not. What was your specific task, what was the order that you were issued with? What was your job along that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our job, our task, was to secure that road for traffic, to protect the villages lying beyond the communication, and Bratunac itself, from possible attacks of the army of BiH. And that was our sole task that is known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was anything said to you on that occasion with regard to treating POWs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could we now have a look at 4D78, please? And this is an order from the VRS Main Staff dated the 11th of July, 1995. We could go through the orders and the system of command and subordination in relation to this task that related to the road. Unfortunately, we don't have a translation of this document, at least I don't think so. Now I have been told that we do. So there is an English version of this document. Could we scroll down in the English version to the part where MUP is referred to? You have to go to the next page in the English version. Thank you. It's D, second paragraph in the English version. Sir, have a look at the penultimate paragraph in the B/C/S version, which states the following: "In consultation with the responsible MUP organs in Vlasenica, Han Pijesak and Sokolac, use your forces economically to secure control of the communications route and prevent the passage of Muslims from and into the enclave and control of territory in the depth." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Does this reflect what you said a minute ago with regard to your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's have a look at 4D79, a Defence Exhibit. This is an order from Drina Corps command. The date is the same, Your Honours, the 11th of July, 1995. It's the penultimate paragraph in the B/C/S version, the MUP is referred to. It's the second page in the English version. You can see the reference to the MUP, to MUP. Thank you. Sir, here again it states in the Drina Corps document dated the 11th of July, the following -- have a look at the last paragraph. "By arrangement and cooperation with MUP organs in Vlasenica, Han Pijesak, Sokolac and Zvornik, and by sensible deployment of forces ensure control of roads, block the passage of Muslims from and into the enclave and take control over the territory in depth in relation to the road." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could we agree that, in fact, the Drina Corps command immediately after having received an almost identical order from the Main Staff, transformed this into an order that was forwarded to subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's have a look at 4D81 now. Your Honours, while waiting for it to come up on the screen, I can tell you that it is a Prosecution document that we are provided with, it is a regular combat report from the Drina Corps command dated the 13th of July, 1995. Could we have a look at the third page in the B/C/S version, and the last page in the English version. That's it. Thank you. Sir, have a look at the part of the decision that we're interested in, the Drina Corps decision in which states the following: "Use part of your forces with the MUP forces to establish control and ambushes on the routes withdrawal from Muslim groups. And the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje-Milici-Vlasenica road and the Zvornik-Sekovici, and Vlasenica road should be fully secured and should be practicable around the clock, provide security for these roads with patrols and by establishing ambushes at appropriate places for such combat activities." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the stamp that we can see shows that this order was processed on the 13th of July at 2010 hours. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the date, the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you agree that you received such an order from Mr. Borovcanin, an order that concerned your duties at the roads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received an order to secure the roads, and, yes, we could assume it was like this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you were present at the road, that agrees with what is stated in this order by the Drina Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember whether the night between the 12th and the 13th and the 13th and the 14th there were any members of the deserters' unit at this road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean at night? I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to correct something my colleague has just drawn my attention to, the fact the question was, whether between the night on the 12th and the 13th, he was there, on the night between the 13th and the 14th, and it didn't concern his unit, it concerned his presence, not the presence of the deserters' unit. I would like to say that for the sake of the transcript. Everything else is fine. Thank you. Now let's have a look at 4D84. While waiting for that document, I'd like to, again, repeat that this is a regular combat report, from the Drina Corps, dated the 14th of July, 1995. And let's focus on the decision, the last page both in the B/C/S and in the English version. It's page 2 in the English version. It's the next page in the B/C/S version too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a Drina Corps order, dated the 14th of July, 1995. And in the decision of the 14th of July, have a look at the bottom. The order was processed at 1945, at the end of that day, and it states that the task was practically the same. "Use part of the forces together with MUP forces to check the territory and the depth and to detect, block, capture and disarm the routed Muslim forces. Protect the population and property." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is that the task you were assigned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Since we have this document before us now, I would also like to ask you whether you know that there were members of the army engaged in this task too because it says, "use part of the forces in cooperation with MUP forces"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, as far as I know, that's the case, but as to where they were located, which area, believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, and let's now see 4D85 to conclude. While waiting for it to appear on the screens, Your Honours, I would like to point out that this is a regular combat report from the Drina Corps dated the 15th of July, 1995. So it's on the following day, the day after the one that the witness has been discussing. Let's have a look at the first page in the B/C/S version, please. And it's the second page, paragraph 3, in the English version. Thank you. And this document states the following, sir. Have a look at the third paragraph from the bottom in the B/C/S version. It states the following: "Measures have been taken with the MUP and MUP special units to increase security along these roads and to secure internal traffic for the needs of our units." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This is an order dated the 15th of July or, rather, it is a regular combat report dated the 15th of July. Let me correct myself. Does it reflect what you were involved in when you established ambushes and went on patrol, et cetera, during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, on the 15th, we were still securing the road. There could have been ambushes at the road, et cetera. I believe that we were providing security for the road though.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that security was provided through patrols that patrolled the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about the patrols, but I know these people were by the road, and I think by the 16th the patrols started. At least as far as we are concerned at the roads.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's today's transcript, page 14, lines 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what time it was on the 15th of July, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was around the 15th of July, and I think it was in the morning, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. With some hindsight -- Mr. Thayer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Mr. President. I think the parties can -- perhaps we can agree that there is a -- something missing as far as I can see in the transcript. What's missing is the specific reference as to who my learned friend was referring to being in the centre for the public security at Zvornik from 9.00 and from 11.15 or 11.00 or 12.00 the same day. I believe I know who he is talking about, I just don't see it in the transcript and it's not reflected in the answer as well. So we can clarify that, I think it may be worth taking up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. President. I appreciate the intervention. That's absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you can proceed. In the meantime, Madam Usher is going to go through the transcript and see which parts -- at least I can remember two parts where we need to redact this. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let's conclude this part of my questioning. Do you accept the possibility that this took place on the 14th of July in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept the possibility that this may have happened on another date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. This concludes this part of my questioning. Now, let us go to Exhibit 4D87. And before we have it on the screen in the e-court, Your Honours, I would like to say this: It goes for a memo or a letter of the deputy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you proceed with this new point, Mr. Thayer's intervention called for a clarification, which you haven't addressed. If I can refer you to page 76, line 9 to line 20, to line 3 on page 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honours. I will try to clarify this matter through my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, when recently I asked you whether it was possible, and the name was missing in the transcript, my question was, is it possible that Ljubomir Borovcanin, on the date in question, on the 15th, pursuant to witness statements that we have here, that he, from 9.00 in the morning attended a meeting at the public security centre in Zvornik and from 11.00 onwards at the Zvornik Brigade. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is possible. That is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this sufficient, Your Honour? Then I would continue with my line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In the meantime, we have this document on the screen. Now I would like to ask you to take a look at this document. It is a query by the rear organ of the Drina Corps, specifying that in the territory of Srebrenica and Bratunac, a MUP unit is deployed and that the matter of feeding them is a contentious issue that should been regulated. And the question or the query is, who is in charge of supplying them with food, these members of MUP, while they are in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let us go back to Article 14 of the law on the application of the internal affairs law. That is Exhibit -- the exhibit that we used, P00725. So P00725. Article 14, paragraph 4 on the law on the application of the interim affairs of law in periods of immediate threat of war or state of war. Article 14 is on the next page. Thank you. This is fine. So the penultimate and the last paragraph is what we're interested in. Sir, take a look at paragraph 4 of Article 14, which reads, "In the zone in which they are carrying out combat operations, the commander to whom a police unit has been resubordinated shall provide logistic support for the police unit in the same way as to the other units of the army of Republika Srpska." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Those days, in terms of logistics, were you supplied through the Drina Corps logistics units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who supplied us. Believe me, I know that we were billeted at a school building. I cannot recall whom we received food from. It would be only logical to be supplied or given all the supplies that we needed from them in terms of food, fuel, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to focus on paragraph 3 of Article 14, which reads: "Police units resubordinated to the army of RS in a certain zone shall be used only for combat operations established in advance by the commander in chief or the ministry of -- Minister of the Interior." Can you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Is it known to you personally, having it in mind the order dated 10th of July, 1995, whereby you were given this combat task, whether it was determined how the army may use you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am concerned, and as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What were your uses, if this is known to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could be used to perform tasks through Mr. Borovcanin, to be given a task from him at the level of Drina Corps, and to carry out such specified tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So Mr. Borovcanin would be the person relaying that order into the MUP line of command from the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me conclude. Is it known to you that at that time in July 1995, and within the scope of that combat task, whether all platoon leaders in the so-called deserters' unit, were they professionals or were some platoon leaders appointed from the ranks of the so-called deserters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were appointed from the ranks of the deserters and platoon leaders were chosen from the ranks of the instructors. That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So the platoon leaders were also chosen from the ranks of the deserters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-160 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, let us discuss the activities of your unit during the search of the terrain, and this is a new subject, Your Honour, and we have some documents to scrutinise, and maybe this would be the right time to adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's what we are going to do. We will adjourn, continue tomorrow at 9.00. Sorry, at 2.15 in the afternoon. I wish we would transfer to the morning. Have a nice afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 13th day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
